connectionSpecification.description: Reads the collections of a MongoDB database: full refresh, or incremental by a cursor field.

allow_missing_cursor.description: Incremental streams only. When false, an incremental read fails while any document of the collection has the cursor field null or missing. When true, those documents are skipped on every read and each read logs their count.
allow_missing_cursor.title: Skip documents without a cursor value

oneOf.description: MongoDB Atlas-hosted cluster configured as a replica set

auth_source.description: The database that holds the user. Empty: the authSource of the connection string, else admin.
auth_source.title: Authentication Source

connection_string.description: A mongodb:// URI, with several hosts separated by commas for a replica set, or a mongodb+srv:// URI whose SRV and TXT records list the hosts and options. Options in the URI (replicaSet, tls, readPreference, authMechanism, ...) apply. Leave the user name and password out and set them below.
connection_string.title: Connection String

database.description: The database whose collections are synced.
database.title: Database Name

username.description: The user to log in as. Empty: no authentication, or the user named in the connection string.
username.title: Username

discover_sample_size.description: How many documents of each collection discover samples to infer the collection's schema. Between 1 and 100000. Fields seen in no sampled document are not part of the schema.
discover_sample_size.title: Document discovery sample size

tls_ca_certificate.description: PEM certificate of the CA that signed the server certificates. Setting it turns TLS on. Empty: the CAs trusted by the connector image, and TLS as the connection string says (on for mongodb+srv://).
tls_ca_certificate.title: TLS CA Certificate

tunnel_method.description: Whether to initiate an SSH tunnel before connecting to the database, and if so, which kind of authentication to use.
No ssh tunnel needed to connect to database

ssh_key.description: OS-level user account ssh key credentials in PEM or OpenSSH format (RSA, ECDSA or Ed25519)
ssh_key.title: SSH Private Key

tunnel_host.description: Hostname of the jump server host that allows inbound ssh tunnel.
tunnel_host.title: SSH Tunnel Jump Server Host

tunnel_host_key.description: Public host keys of the jump server, one per line, each in authorized_keys format ("ssh-ed25519 AAAA...") or as a known_hosts line ("bastion.example.com ssh-ed25519 AAAA..."); the whole output of ssh-keyscan works. The tunnel is refused when the server presents none of them. When empty, the host key is not verified.
tunnel_host_key.title: SSH Host Key

tunnel_method.description: Connect through a jump server tunnel host using username and ssh key

tunnel_port.description: Port on the proxy/jump server that accepts inbound ssh connections.
tunnel_port.title: SSH Connection Port

tunnel_user.description: OS-level username for logging into the jump server host.
tunnel_user.title: SSH Login Username
